rationale: Both use memoised recursion over sorted count tuples. A is better documented and better reasoned. A module docstring lays out the price table, and the helper's docstring explains why it only needs to take a group of size g from the g most plentiful titles. That keeps the search to five branches per state. B tries every one of the 31 bitmasks, using bit-twiddling, a manual validity flag and bin().count('1'). That works, but it is noisier and explores many redundant choices. A's single nested min(... tuple(sorted(...))) expression is denser than ideal and could have been split into a helper. B's use of Counter in total is a nice idiomatic touch. On balance A's clearer intent and leaner search make it the better solution.
